result.strongest_objection:
R3 as written makes the origin-free SSHSIG format depend on WebAuthn enrolment state. For a loopback Host, the only Origins the POST admits are `http://localhost:

` and active passkey origins; the doc itself marks which `Host` the daemon sees behind `tailscale serve` UNVERIFIED (§2.3, R9). So an operator who opens the card via the tailnet HTTPS name while the daemon sees `127.0.0.1:7644` gets 403 CrossOrigin on every SSHSIG POST unless a passkey happens to be enrolled at that origin — an SSH key has no origin binding, so nothing in the artifact justifies blocking it, and the parent's A3 sentence puts both formats on the card. The doc's 'Both pass' claim (§2.3) is true only for the Host allowlist, not for this composite flow: no RG1 or RT8 row, no residual (R9 covers the passkey path only), and no §10 step (§10.5 runs SSHSIG Mac-local only) covers the case, so the loop builds and the operator discovers a hard-blocked approval path at the attended exit run.
result.catch: Two things. (1) Decide and pin the R3 rule for non-localhost origins: is 'an active passkey's origin' meant to vouch origins for SSHSIG too? Add the (Host: `127.0.0.1:7644`, Origin: `https://<ts.net>`, no ts.net-enrolled passkey) row to RG1 and RT8 and a tailnet SSHSIG step to §10.5. (2) Three load-bearing premises about existing machinery have no V-log row: that `DecidedMintRequests("", 20)` treats an empty `approvedBy` as 'all decided rows' rather than a filter (§2.3 — if it filters, the decision list, parent §2.4 step 4, is silently always empty); that the at-start 'admission' in `--await` is non-consuming, i.e. where the once-only C6 consume actually sits relative to the minter's 'steps 2–6' (AW1's 'row recorded mid-wait', M2 and XA1 all require the request to stay pending during the wait, yet nothing in §1 or §14 pins the consume's location); and that `SignedApproval.Binds(digest, challenge, expiry)` exists as a callable (R12).
result.proposed_fix:
Rewrite R3 as: 'Origin present, and its host is a host the R2 allowlist already admits — i.e. the request's own Host, `localhost:

`/`127.0.0.1:

`, or an active passkey's origin host — so a card opened at any Host-admitted origin can POST either format' (R4/R5 still bind; the artifact's law check is origin-independent, so this adds no new authority surface). Add residual R10: 'SSHSIG over the tailnet name depends on the Host `tailscale serve` forwards (R9); under the rewritten-Host case only the passkey-origin arm admits it, so a tailnet SSHSIG approval requires a passkey enrolled at that origin — the card shows the 403's class and reason, and §10 records the observed behaviour.' Add RG1/RT8 rows for (loopback Host, ts.net Origin, no ts.net passkey) under both readings, and a §10.5 tailnet-SSH step. Add verification rows: V23 `grep -n 'func DecidedMintRequests' -A25 host/store/mint_requests.go` plus the `approve.go:337-352` call site, showing what `--list --decided` passes and that an empty approver returns all rows; V24 pinning the once-only consume's location (grep the consume in `mint_requests.go`/`approve.go` relative to `provisionEpisode`), so AW1's mid-wait-record premise is verified rather than asserted; V25 `grep -n 'func .*Binds' host/approval/*.go` proving R12's method exists with that signature.

result.strongest_objection: The doc's central security property — by-construction #2 and T4/T13, i.e. 'the page computes the digest and the 90-byte SignedMessage itself with crypto.subtle, byte-equal to approval.SignedMessage/MessageHash' — rests on an UNVERIFIED browser-capability premise that the verification log falsely claims was measured. R5 (§11) says 'fetch POST headers, crypto.subtle and Notifications … (Chrome 157 measured, V17)', but V17's logged probe (/tmp/w383-designer/hdr/probe.mjs) measured only the same-origin POST headers and the cross-origin preflight; its Observed column contains no crypto.subtle digest output, no Notification permission read, and no byte-level comparison of a JS-reconstructed message against Go's approval.SignedMessage/MessageHash golden bytes. Every other load-bearing premise in this doc (writer discipline V8, harness pass V15, preflight behavior V17) is evidence-backed; the one premise the entire 'what you see is what you sign' defense depends on is asserted and miscited. Under gate 1, an asserted premise dressed as a measured one is a reject, however likely it is to be true (WebCrypto at http://localhost almost certainly works — the point is the doc's own standard, set by V17 and D-WORLD-109, says exactly this class of browser-behavior claim gets probed at design time, and the guards R3–R5 were themselves designed from such a probe). XA1/XA2 would catch a failure in sprint 3, but that is the build phase judging a design-time premise this doc had the means and the precedent to measure before freeze.
result.catch:
Fix three cells: (1) §11 R5's parenthetical '(Chrome 157 measured, V17)' — V17 as logged supports only the fetch-header/preflight half; as written it also certifies crypto.subtle and Notifications, which the probe never touched. (2) §14 V17's Observed column contains nothing about WebCrypto, the 90-byte reconstruction, or Notification permission state, yet §2.7 step 3, §5 by-construction #2, and T4/T13 all load on page-side SHA-256 and byte-exact 'world-approval/v1'‖0x00‖digest‖nonce‖u64be(expiry) assembly in JS (hex decode of digest/nonce, u64 BE encoding of expiry — all new in A3; A2's page took a server-computed challenge per V16). (3) A sibling spec gap worth fixing in the same pass: §2.4 R3's Origin rule as written admits 'http://localhost:

or an active passkey's origin', which does not literally cover a card served from and posting to http://127.0.0.1:

with no passkey enrolled at that exact origin — the self-origin cell for 127.0.0.1 is unspecified (RG1's test table lists 'localhost:' but never '127.0.0.1:

self-origin'), so the pristine loopback path could 403.
result.proposed_fix:
Extend the existing throwaway probe (same discipline as V17, kept out of the repo) and add one verification-log row. In /tmp/w383-designer/hdr/, serve a page over http://127.0.0.1: in headless Chrome (temp profile, virtual authenticator) that: (a) computes crypto.subtle.digest('SHA-256', bytes) for a fixture request and compares to a Go-printed golden digest; (b) reconstructs the exact 90-byte message via TextEncoder + Uint8Array concat + DataView.setBigUint64(false) and hashes it, comparing byte-for-byte to golden output from approval.SignedMessage and approval.MessageHash; (c) reads Notification.permission and the result of a gesture-driven requestPermission. Log the observed matches as a new V23 row, and reword §11 R5 to: 'Safari and Firefox behaviour … UNVERIFIED (Chrome 157 measured, V17 headers/preflight, V23 WebCrypto/message-assembly/Notification)'. Also amend §2.4 R3's first disjunct to 'Origin equal to the request's own origin (scheme http, host exactly the Host header value, limited to the loopback allowlist of §2.3) or an active passkey's origin', and add the '127.0.0.1:

self-origin, no enrolled passkey' row to RG1's table. No design mechanism changes; this is one probe script, one log row, one corrected cross-reference, and one guard-spec sentence.

result.strongest_objection: The claim that the card shows the full request is contradicted by the specified renderer. §1.2 says the signed canonical request includes repo, git binary, credentials_db, mcp_config, task and daemon, but §2.7's display list omits these fields. Hashing all the bytes does not establish that the operator saw all mint-relevant inputs. This leaves §5.2's 'what the operator saw is what was signed' argument and T9's full-request mitigation unsupported.
result.catch: XA1 checks only that displayed grants equal the request's grants. It would pass even if the card concealed a changed executable, repository, configuration path or daemon reference.
result.proposed_fix: Replace §2.7 step 2 with: 'After verifying the digest, render every field of the decoded canonical request with explicit labels, including repo, git binary, credentials_db, mcp_config, task and daemon, and every grant field. A concise summary may precede this complete view, but approval remains disabled if any canonical field cannot be represented.' Extend XA1 with distinct sentinel values for every canonical field and assert that all appear in the rendered request details before approval. Narrow §5.2 to distinguish cryptographic byte binding from completeness of the operator-visible presentation.
